t: Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Technique: Precision Practice
description:
Where Method One is the whole procedure, the Precision Technique is the Signature system's way of doing the delicate middle of the work well. It is a practice discipline for spec catalog pending patents: small, exact, repeatable moves that compound into quality.

The technique scores every attempt on three axes: exactness, consistency, and finish. Exactness measures whether the piece matches its specification. Consistency measures whether repeated attempts match each other. Finish measures whether the piece is complete and presentable. A Signature practitioner drills until all three axes read high.

The demonstration below scores sample attempts on the three axes and grades them, the same way the measurement scale grades real work.
disclaimer: Signature-original work created in the Signature system. Never presented as public record.

# Signature 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents' - 'Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Technique: Precision Practice'
# Property of Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Signature-original demonstration.
# Save as demo.py and run: python3 demo.py

def score_attempt(exactness, consistency, finish):
    total = (exactness + consistency + finish) / 3.0
    grade = "master" if total >= 9 else "journeyman" if total >= 7 else "apprentice"

          "=>", total, "(" + grade + ")")

description:
The Signature spec catalog pending patents Protocol turns Method One into a checklist: numbered steps, each with a verification, so two different people following the protocol produce the same quality of result. Protocols are the Signature system's answer to 'how do I do it right the first time.'

Each step states its action, its check, and its fallback. The action is what you do. The check proves you did it. The fallback says what to do if the check fails. A protocol with no fallbacks is a wish; this one has fallbacks for every step.

The demonstration below runs the protocol's steps against a sample task, printing each check result.

# Signature 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents' - 'Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Protocol: The Step-by-Step Procedure'
# Property of Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Signature-original demonstration.
# Save as demo.py and run: python3 demo.py

DOMAIN = 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents'

STEPS = [
    ("Prepare", "materials listed", "gather missing materials"),
    ("Shape", "pattern slots filled", "re-apply the Reusable Blueprint"),
    ("Stress", "measurement scale reads pass", "drill the Precision Technique"),
    ("Ship", "working version runs", "repair the working version first"),
]

def run_protocol(task):
    log = []

t: Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Reference Implementation
description:
The Reference Implementation is the Signature system's canonical working code for spec catalog pending patents: a small, readable program that demonstrates the core ideas correctly. It is the implementation other implementations are compared against, and it runs as-is.

The implementation models a tiny spec catalog pending patents catalog: records can be added, searched by keyword, and ranked by ladder. It is deliberately small — under a hundred lines — so a student can read the whole thing in one sitting and understand every line.

The demonstration below builds the catalog, files three sample records, and runs two searches, printing the results.

program:
# Signature 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents' - 'Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Reference Implementation'
# Property of Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Signature-original demonstration.
# Save as demo.py and run: python3 demo.py

DOMAIN = 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents'

class SigCatalog:
    def __init__(self):
        self.records = []
    def add(self, title, ladder):
        self.records.append({"title": title, "ladder": ladder})
    def search(self, keyword):
        kw = keyword.lower()
        return [r for r in self.records if kw in r["title"].lower()]
    def by_ladder(self, rank):
        return [r for r in self.records if r["ladder"] == rank]

cat = SigCatalog()
cat.add("Signature " + DOMAIN + " field guide", 1)
cat.add("Signature " + DOMAIN + " method one", 2)
cat.add("Signature " + DOMAIN + " master work", 3)

description:

The demonstration below is a miniature of the AI's lookup behavior: a tiny question bank answered from archive-style records.

# Signature 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents' - 'Signature Spec Catalog Pending Patents Archive-Aware AI Integration'
# Property of Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Signature-original demonstration.
# Save as demo.py and run: python3 demo.py

DOMAIN = 'Spec Catalog Pending Patents'

BANK = [
    ("what is a signature method", "A named, repeatable Signature-original procedure for " + DOMAIN.lower() + "."),
    ("what is the teaching ladder", "Simple first, compounded second, complex last: ladder ranks 1, 2, 3."),
    ("how is work scored", "On the Measurement Scale: originality, clarity, completeness, craft, honest labeling."),
    ("what does compounding mean", "Each generation improves on every axis of the last: Mark I proves, Mark II refines, Mark III masters."),
]

def answer(q):
    ql = q.lower()
    best, best_hit = "I would route that to the wider network.", 0
    for question, ans in BANK:
        hit = sum(1 for w in ql.split() if w in question)
        if hit > best_hit:
            best, best_hit = ans, hit
    return best

for q in ["How is work scored?", "What is compounding?", "What is the teaching ladder?"]:
    print("Q:", q)
    print("A:", answer(q))
print("Archive-aware lookup miniature ready for", DOMAIN)
